notes: Collected from the date-sorted mail-archive.com xz-devel index (msg00509-msg00673) plus Andres Freund's oss-security post on openwall.com; each text was machine-checked as an exact substring of the fetched message body (quoted reply lines removed, hard line wraps and runs of whitespace collapsed to single spaces). Original spelling is preserved.

messages.author: Alexander Bluhm
messages.subject: [xz-devel] [PATCH] xz: Avoid fchown(2) failure.
messages.text: OpenBSD does not allow to change the group of a file if the user does not belong to this group. In contrast to Linux, OpenBSD also fails if the new group is the same as the old one. Do not call fchown(2) in this case, it would change nothing anyway.

messages.author: Lasse Collin
messages.subject: [xz-devel] XZ Utils 5.3.2alpha
messages.text: XZ Utils 5.3.2alpha is available at <https://tukaani.org/xz/>. Here is an extract from the NEWS file: This release was made on short notice so that recent erofs-utils can be built with LZMA support without needing a snapshot from xz.git.

messages.author: Jia Tan
messages.subject: [xz-devel] [PATCH] xz: Added .editorconfig file for simple style guide encouragement
messages.text: This patch adds a .editorconfig to the root directory. The .editorconfig file integrates into most text editors and IDE's to enforce basic styling. I chose the configurations from the project's current styling.

messages.author: Jia Tan
messages.subject: [xz-devel] [PATCH] xz: Converted test framework to use Seatest
messages.text: This patch converts the existing test framework to use an open source C testing framework called Seatest. For now, I only converted the existing tests. I wanted your feedback before I used this framework to add new tests. Let me know what changes you would like to see.

messages.author: Jia Tan
messages.subject: [xz-devel] [PATCH] xz: Multithreaded mode now always uses stream_encoder_mt to ensure reproducible builds
messages.text: This patch addresses the issues with reproducible builds when using multithreaded xz. Previously, specifying --threads=1 instead of --threads=[n>1] creates different output. Now, setting any number of threads forces multithreading mode, even if there is only 1 worker thread.

messages.author: Jia Tan
messages.subject: [xz-devel] XZ memory usage limiting for --threads=0
messages.text: This patch adds memory limiting in xz when --threads=0 is specified.

messages.author: Jean-Pierre Giraud

messages.text: Please find attached the french translation of the xz-utils manpage done by "bubu" and proofread by the debian-l10n-french mailing list contributors. I think that this new translation could be included in a future release.

messages.author: Jia Tan
messages.subject: Re: [xz-devel] [PATCH v3] liblzma: Add multi-threaded decoder
messages.text: Thanks for doing this testing! Looks like the threading scales fairly well on large files like this. I don't have a machine with resources like this, so I am glad you were able to do this. I started writing tests in the new framework and I found one bug and one issue.

messages.author: Lasse Collin
messages.subject: [xz-devel] xzgrep security fix for XZ Utils <= 5.2.5, 5.3.2alpha (ZDI-CAN-16587)
messages.text: Malicious filenames can make xzgrep to write to arbitrary files or (with a GNU sed extension) lead to arbitrary code execution. xzgrep from XZ Utils versions up to and including 5.2.5 are affected. 5.3.1alpha and 5.3.2alpha are affected as well. This patch works for all of them.

messages.author: Andres Freund
messages.subject: backdoor in upstream xz/liblzma leading to ssh server compromise
messages.text: After observing a few odd symptoms around liblzma (part of the xz package) on Debian sid installations over the last weeks (logins with ssh taking a lot of CPU, valgrind errors) I figured out the answer: The upstream xz repository and the xz tarballs have been backdoored. At first I thought this was a compromise of debian's package, but it turns out to be upstream.
